funFact: Real starfish can regrow an arm — your body does its best repair work when you rest, too!
story: At the bottom of a quiet lagoon, a little starfish spread out on the soft sand and let the gentle waves rock it to sleep.
description: Lie on your back and spread out like a big starfish! ⭐ Arms wide, legs wide, eyes softly closed. Let the floor hold you like warm sand. Shhh... melt a little more with every breath.

funFact: Butterflies rest with their wings open to soak up warm sunshine — just like you in this pose!
story: A sleepy butterfly landed on a sunny leaf, let its wings fall open, and took the coziest nap in the garden.
description: Lie on your back, press the bottoms of your feet together, and let your knees fall open like butterfly wings. 🦋 Rest your hands on your belly. Feel it rise... and fall... as you breathe slow and soft.

benefits: Stretches the front of the legs
funFact: Even the bravest heroes rest — this pose is how yoga heroes recharge their superpowers.
story: After saving the day, a young hero leaned back onto a mountain of cushions, took a giant breath, and let every muscle rest.
description: Kneel and sit between your heels, then slowly lean back onto a big stack of pillows. 🦸 Ease back only as far as feels comfy — pillows are your hero headquarters! Breathe slow and feel the front of your legs stretch.
safetyNote: Only with a grown-up nearby and a tall pillow stack. Come up right away if knees or back complain — sit-up hero is just as strong.

funFact: Babies really do grab their feet like this — it keeps their hips happy and healthy!
story: A giggly baby discovered its own feet for the very first time and rocked side to side with joy.
description: Lie on your back and hug your knees in. Now grab the outsides of your feet and let your knees drop wide. 👶 Rock gently side to side like a happy baby — wheee! Keep breathing and smiling.

funFact: Gently squeezing your knees to your chest gives your low back a tiny massage from the floor.
story: A little koala missed its mama tree, so it gave itself the biggest, warmest hug — and felt cozy all over.
description: Lie on your back and pull both knees in toward your chest. Wrap your arms around them — biggest self-hug ever! 🤗 Rock gently side to side and whisper a slow breath out... ahhh.

benefits: Stretches the back of the leg
funFact: The muscles behind your leg are called hamstrings — they love slow, easy stretches like this one.
story: A tiny explorer sent one leg up like a flagpole to say hello to the sky, then switched flags to be fair.
description: Lie on your back and hug one knee in. Hold your big toe (or your leg!) and slowly stretch that foot up to the sky. 🦶 Keep the other leg long and lazy on the floor. Breathe... then switch sides!

funFact: Yogis use straps like lassos — the strap does the reaching so your body can just relax.
story: A gentle cowpoke lassoed the moon with a soft rope, then lay back and let the moon hold the rope steady.
description: Lie on your back and loop a soft strap or towel around one foot. Send that foot up to the sky and hold the strap like reins — the strap does the work! 🪢 Shoulders melt into the floor. Slow breaths, then switch legs.

funFact: Crocodiles can lie still for hours — they are the champion resters of the river!
story: A sleepy crocodile floated in the warm shallows, resting its chin on a log and breathing slow, bubbly breaths.
description: Lie on your tummy and stack your hands under your forehead like a pillow. 🐊 Let your legs go long and floppy. Feel your belly press into the floor with every slow breath — you're a resting river croc!

funFact: Mice curl into tiny balls to stay warm — curling up helps people feel calm and safe too.
story: A little mouse tiptoed into its cozy burrow, curled up small as a cotton ball, and listened to the quiet.
description: Kneel down, sit back on your heels, and fold forward until your forehead rests on the floor. 🐭 Tuck your arms alongside you like tiny mouse paws. Be squeak-quiet and breathe soft, slow breaths.

funFact: A turtle's shell is part of its skeleton — it carries its cozy bedroom everywhere it goes!
story: A tired turtle tucked its head into its shell, sighed a happy sigh, and dreamed of slow adventures.
description: Start in a kneeling fold with your forehead down. Now reach your arms back beside your legs, palms up, and imagine your rounded back is a turtle shell. 🐢 Snuggle in and breathe slowwwly inside your shell.

funFact: Birds line their nests with the softest things they can find — feathers, moss, even fluff!
story: A baby bird built the fluffiest nest in the forest and sank into it, safe and warm, as the stars came out.
description: Put a big pillow between your knees, then fold forward and hug it like a cloud. 🪺 Turn one cheek onto the pillow and let your whole body go soft. Switch cheeks halfway. Coziest nest ever!

funFact: Fish breathe with gills, but this pose helps YOUR lungs open up like big balloons.
story: A shiny fish floated up to the sunny surface, opened its fins wide, and let the warm light fill its chest.
description: Place a folded blanket or pillow behind you and lie back so it props up your upper back. 🐟 Let your arms flop open, chest floating up like a fish in sunshine. Big slow breaths — feel your chest open wiiiide.
safetyNote: Keep head and neck resting comfortably on support. Skip if your neck feels achy today.

funFact: Cats sleep up to 16 hours a day — they are the world's best nappers!
story: A fluffy cat found a sunbeam on the rug, curled into a perfect circle, and purred itself to sleep.
description: Lie on your side and curl up like a napping kitty. 🐱 Bend your knees toward your chest and rest your head on your arm or a pillow. Purr a soft breath out... purrrr... and let your whole body get heavy.

funFact: When you squeeze your muscles and then let go, they relax even more than before — scientists use this trick too!
story: A jolly snowman stood stiff in the winter sun, then slowly, happily melted into a peaceful puddle of snow.
description: Stand or kneel tall and freeze stiff like a snowman — squeeze everything! ⛄ Now the sun comes out... slooowly melt down, down, down until you're a puddle lying on the floor. Let every last snowflake go soft.

funFact: Clouds can weigh as much as a hundred elephants, yet they float — because they're spread so softly thin.
story: Two friends lay in a meadow finding dragon shapes and ice-cream castles in the drifting clouds above.
description: Lie on your back with your hands behind your head, elbows wide. ☁️ Close your eyes and imagine puffy clouds drifting by. What shapes do you see? Breathe as slow as a cloud floats.

funFact: Yoga teachers call pillows and blankets 'props' — they let your body rest without working at all.
story: A sleepy mountaineer climbed a mountain made entirely of blankets and decided the summit was the perfect spot for a snooze.
description: Stack blankets or pillows into a soft mountain, then lean back on it so your head is highest. 🏔️ Arms melt to your sides, legs go long. You climbed it — now rest on the tippy-top and breathe.

funFact: Belly breathing tells your brain 'all is well' — it's like a secret calm button in your tummy.
story: A little balloon dreamed of flying, so every breath it puffed itself rounder and rounder until it floated over the fair.
description: Lie on your back and put both hands (or a stuffy!) on your belly. 🎈 Breathe in through your nose and blow your belly up like a balloon... then let it sloooowly deflate. Fill it up again — big, round, gentle.

funFact: Bhramari is named after a black Indian bee — humming really can help your body relax!
story: A fuzzy bumblebee hummed its favorite one-note song all the way home, and the whole garden felt sleepy and safe.
description: Sit comfy and gently cover your ears with your fingers. Breathe in through your nose... and hum out looong like a bee: mmmmmm! 🐝 Feel the buzz tickle inside your head. Hum again, soft and slow.

funFact: If you cup a seashell over your ear, you hear an ocean sound — your ujjayi breath makes the same waves!
story: A child held a seashell to one ear and discovered the ocean lived inside their own breath all along.
description: Sit tall and breathe in through your nose. Now breathe out through your nose while gently squeezing the back of your throat — hear that soft ocean sound? 🌊 Shhhh-ahhh, like waves rolling in and out. Listen to your own sea.

funFact: Long, slow breaths out are the fastest way to tell your whole body it's time to relax.
story: On a birthday made of quiet wishes, one gentle candle flickered — and a soft, slow breath made the wish come true.
description: Sit comfy and hold up one finger — that's your candle. 🕯️ Breathe in through your nose, then blow out slooowly, so gently the flame only flickers. Try again: can you make the world's longest, softest blow?

funFact: Smelling something nice and slow naturally makes your breath deep — your nose is a calm-down helper!
story: In a garden of a thousand flowers, a small explorer stopped at every single one for a long, happy sniff.
description: Cup your hands like they're holding a beautiful flower. 🌸 Breathe in through your nose — mmm, smell that! Then sigh the breath out through your mouth — ahhh. Pick a new imaginary flower and sniff again.

funFact: Snakes hiss by pushing air through a special little tube — your hiss uses your teeth!
story: A friendly garden snake warmed itself on a rock, letting out long happy hisses that sounded just like the breeze.
description: Lie on your tummy and prop up on your forearms like a resting snake. 🐍 Breathe in through your nose... then hiss it out long and soft: ssssssss! How long can your gentle hiss go? Try three slow hisses.

funFact: On a clear dark night you can see about two thousand stars — that's a lot of slow breaths!
story: A drowsy astronomer counted stars instead of sheep: one twinkle, one breath... and drifted into dreams by star number ten.
description: Lie back and close your eyes under your imaginary night sky. ✨ Breathe in and picture one star lighting up... breathe out and whisper 'one'. Next breath, 'two'. Count your stars all the way to ten, slow as moonlight.

benefits: Relaxes one part at a time
funFact: Noticing each body part one by one is called a body scan — it's a real relaxation superpower.
story: After a big day of beeping and building, a helpful robot pressed its own sleep button and powered down piece by piece.
description: Lie on your back — you're a robot at bedtime! 🤖 Beep! Power down your feet... they go still. Beep! Legs off... belly off... arms off... Last one: beep, face soft, systems resting. Zzzz-whirrr.

funFact: When your muscles go floppy on purpose, your brain gets the message to relax too.
story: A well-loved rag doll flopped onto its toy-shelf seat after a day of adventures, soft and smiling and completely relaxed.
description: Sit criss-cross and let your whole top half go floppy — head heavy, arms dangly, back softly rounded. 🪆 You're a cozy rag doll! Sway a teeny bit side to side. Then slowly roll back up, one floppy bit at a time.

funFact: Butterflies fold their wings up when they sleep — folding forward helps you feel sleepy-calm too.
story: As the moon rose over the meadow, a butterfly folded its wings, bowed its head to a petal pillow, and fell fast asleep.
description: Sit with the soles of your feet together, knees out like wings. 🦋 Now let your butterfly fall asleep: fold slowly forward and let your head hang heavy. Rest there, breathing soft nighttime breaths.

funFact: Inside a real cocoon, a caterpillar rests and transforms into a butterfly — rest helps you grow too!
story: A tired caterpillar wrapped itself in the softest silk blanket, whispering, 'When I wake up, I'll have wings.'
description: Lie on your side and hug your knees in snug. Wrap a blanket around you if you have one — you're a caterpillar in a cocoon! 🐛 Close your eyes and rest. Imagine growing beautiful wings while you breathe.

funFact: Some rocks have sat perfectly still for millions of years — talk about champion stillness!
story: A smooth river rock watched clouds, storms, and seasons drift past, staying peaceful and still through it all.
description: Kneel and sit back on your heels with a tall, quiet back. 🪨 Rest your hands on your legs and be still as a mountain rock. Can you feel your breath moving while everything else stays steady? So strong, so calm.

funFact: Your head weighs about as much as a bowling ball — your neck deserves gentle thank-you circles!
story: A drowsy owl drew slow, lazy circles with its beak, saying goodnight to every corner of the forest.
description: Sit tall and let your chin drop softly toward your chest. 🙆 Now roll your head slooowly to one shoulder, back to the middle, then to the other shoulder — like drawing a smile with your chin. Gentle and dreamy, no rush.

benefits: Stretches the side of the neck
funFact: A giraffe's neck is six feet long but has the same number of neck bones as yours — seven!
story: A gentle giraffe leaned its long neck against a warm acacia tree, sighing happily as the sunset painted the sky.
description: Sit tall like a graceful giraffe. 🦒 Let your right ear float down toward your right shoulder — feel the soft stretch on the other side. Breathe there... then float your head up and tilt to the left. Long, happy giraffe neck!

funFact: Shoulders often creep up toward your ears when you're busy — rolling them tells them to take a vacation.
story: At the sleepy evening fair, the ferris wheel turned slower and slower, giving every rider one last dreamy loop.
description: Sit or kneel tall. Lift your shoulders up to your ears... roll them back... and melt them down. 🎡 Slow, round circles like a ferris wheel at closing time. Three loops back, then three loops forward. Ahh, floaty shoulders!

funFact: Eagles wrap their wings tight around themselves to stay warm on windy cliff tops.
story: A young eagle folded its great wings snugly around itself and watched the stars twinkle over the mountains.
description: Sit comfy and give yourself a hug — now wiggle your arms so they wrap around each other, palms reaching toward each other. 🦅 Lift your elbows a little and feel the stretch between your shoulder blades. Breathe... unwrap... and swap which arm is on top!

funFact: This pose's name comes from how the crossed legs look like a cow's face — moo-velous!
story: A patient cow in a starlit barn reached back to scratch between her shoulders and let out the happiest 'moooo.'
description: Sit tall. Reach one arm up and drop the hand behind your head. Reach the other arm low and sneak its hand up your back. 🐮 Try to have your fingers wave hello — or hold a sock between them! Breathe, then switch sides. Moo!

funFact: Putting your legs up helps the blood in your feet slide back toward your heart — like a lazy river ride.
story: After a day of hopping everywhere, a tired bunny flipped upside-down against a tree and let its feet finally rest.
description: Scoot your bottom close to a wall, then swing your legs up so they rest against it. 🦵 Lie back, arms relaxed, legs tall and lazy. Let your feet take a vacation while you breathe slow, cozy breaths.

funFact: Twists give your spine a gentle squeeze-and-release, like wringing out a soft sponge.
story: A lazy river turned one slow bend to the left, then one slow bend to the right, carrying little boats to dreamland.
description: Lie on your back and hug your knees in. Let both knees fall to one side while your arms stretch wide like a T. 🌀 Look the other way if it feels nice. Breathe... then float your knees over to the other side.

funFact: Crossing your legs in a twist reaches muscles on the side of your hips that regular twists miss.
story: An eagle crossed its talons, tucked its wings, and rocked gently in its nest as the wind sang a lullaby.
description: Lie on your back and cross one leg over the other like cozy pretzel legs. 🦅 Now let both knees drift slowly to one side and stretch your arms wide. Breathe into your back... then switch your leg-cross and twist the other way.

benefits: Opens the front of the body
funFact: Real bridges rest on strong supports — in this pose, a pillow is the support and YOU are the bridge!
story: A little bridge over a quiet stream leaned on its favorite stone pillow and listened to the water gurgle by all night.
description: Lie on your back with knees bent, feet flat. Press into your feet, lift your hips, and slide a pillow or cushion under your bottom. 🌉 Now rest ON the pillow — you're a floating bridge! Arms soft, breath slow.
safetyNote: Keep the support under your hips, not your low back, and slide it out before rolling to your side to get up.

funFact: Swans really do sleep with their heads tucked down into their soft feathers.
story: On a silver lake at dusk, a graceful swan folded forward over one wing and drifted to sleep on the still water.
description: From hands and knees, slide one knee forward behind your wrist and stretch the other leg long behind you. 🦢 Now fold forward and rest your head on your hands or a pillow — a sleeping swan! Breathe softly, then switch legs.

funFact: Puppies do this exact stretch when they wake up from naps — it's called a play-bow!
story: A floppy-eared puppy woke from a nap, stretched its paws way out front, and wagged a slow, happy tail.
description: Start on hands and knees, then walk your paws way forward and melt your chest toward the floor, tail up! 🐶 Rest your forehead down and let your heart sink low. Sigh out a big puppy sigh... woof, that feels good.

funFact: Folding forward over support lets gravity do the stretching while you just relax and breathe.
story: A sleepy elf leaned forward onto a marshmallow pillow at the end of toy-making day and dreamed of jingling bells.
description: Sit with your legs long and place a big pillow on top of them. 🛏️ Take a breath in, sit tall... then fold forward and hug the pillow, resting your head on it. Knees can bend — comfy beats far! Breathe and melt.

funFact: Snails carry their cozy spiral homes everywhere and tuck inside whenever they want quiet time.
story: A small snail finished its slow garden journey, curled into its shiny spiral shell, and whispered, 'Home sweet home.'
description: Sit criss-cross and slowly curl forward, rounding your back into a snail shell shape. 🐌 Let your head bow down and your arms rest wherever they're comfy. Hide in your quiet shell and take five slow snail breaths.

funFact: Lizards lounge on sunny rocks to warm up their bodies — this pose is your sunny rock!
story: A laid-back lizard found the warmest, flattest rock in the canyon and lounged there all afternoon, blinking slowly at the sky.
description: Lie on your tummy and prop up on your forearms, elbows under your shoulders. 🦎 Let your back relax and your head float tall — you're a lizard sunbathing on a warm rock. Slow blink... slow breath... soak up the sunshine.
